MethodDescription: Major and some minor elements are determined by wavelength-dispersive x-ray fluorescence spectrometry (WDXRF) and reported as  element oxides in weight percent. Includes some or all of the following: SiO2, TiO2, Al2O3, Fe2O3, MnO, MgO, CaO, Na2O, K2O, P2O5, BaO, Cr2O3, SrO, V2O5. The sample is fused with lithium metaborate/lithium tetraborate flux and the resultant glass disk is introduced into the WDXRF and irradiated by an x-ray tube. The method also provides a gravimetric loss on ignition (LOI). Data are deemed acceptable when recovery of each major oxide is ±5% at five times the Lower Detection Limit and the calculated percent Relative Standard Deviation (RSD) of duplicate samples is no greater than 5%.
MethodDescriptionSource: U.S. Geological Survey, 2021, Geochemical data generated by projects funded by the USGS Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (ver. 11.0, January 2025): U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9WHRLXH.

MethodDescription: Fifty-five major (except Si and Na), rare earth, and trace elements are determined in geological materials by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) and inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). 0.1 grams of sample is decomposed using a sodium peroxide sinter at 450°C. The resultant cake is leached with water and acidified with nitric acid. After an addition of tartaric acid, aliquots of the digested sample are aspirated into the ICP-AES and the ICP-MS. The concentrations of the optimal elements from the ICP-AES and ICP-MS are determined. Calibration on the ICP-AES is performed by standardizing with digested rock reference materials and a series of multi-element solution standards. The ICP-MS is calibrated with aqueous standards. Internal standards are used to compensate for matrix affects and internal drifts. Some or all of the following elements are analyzed: Al, Ca, Fe, K, Mg, Mn, P, Ti, Ag, As, B, Ba, Be, Bi, Cd, Ce, Co, Cr, Cs, Cu, Dy, Er, Eu, Ga, Gd, Ge, Hf, Ho, In, La, Li, Lu, Mo, Nb, Nd, Ni, Pb, Pr, Rb, Sb, Sc, Sm, Sn, Sr, Ta, Tb, Th, Tl, Tm, U, V, W, Y, Yb, Zn, Zr.
Unit: weight percent (% or pct); parts per million by weight (ppm)
MethodDescriptionSource: J. Azain, U.S. Geological Survey, written commun., 5/20/2025

MethodDescription: Sixty or sixty-one elements (Al, Ca, Fe, K, Mg, P, S, Si, Ti, Ag, As, B, Ba, Be, Bi, Cd, Ce, Co, Cr, Cs, Cu, Dy, Er, Eu, Ga, Gd, Ge, Hf, Ho, In, La, Li, Lu, Mn, Mo, Nb, Nd, Ni, Pb, Pr, Rb, Re, Sb, Sc, Se, Sm, Sn, Sr, Ta, Tb, Te, Th, Tl, Tm, U, V, W, Y, Yb, Zn, Zr) are determined in rocks, minerals, sediments, and soils. Samples are fused at 750°C with sodium peroxide and the fusion cake dissolved in a dilute nitric acid. The resulting solution is analyzed by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) and inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Data are deemed acceptable if recovery for all elements is ±15% at five times the Lower Detection Limit and the calculated Relative Standard Deviation (RSD) of duplicate samples is no greater than 15%.
Unit: weight percent (% or pct); parts per million by weight (ppm)

MethodDescription: Essential (bound) water (H2O_Plus), nonessential water (H2O_Minus), and total water (Total_H2O) determined by heating and weight loss with flux.

Ferrous iron reported as iron(II) oxide or ferrous oxide (FeO) in weight percent, determined by titration (C_TITR_FEO). A 1.0 gram sample is digested by using a mixture of sulfuric and hydrofluoric acids. Boric acid is added to the solution to complex any unreacted HF after the digestion. The sample is quickly cooled and is titrated with a standardized solution of potassium dichromate to determine iron(II) using a sodium diphenylamine sulphonate indicator. Data is deemed acceptable if recovery for total carbon is +/- 15% at five times the Lower Detection Limit and the calculated Relative Standard Deviation (RSD) of duplicate samples is no greater than 15%.

MethodDescription: Sixteen elements (Ce, Dy, Er, Eu, Gd, Ho, La, Lu, Nd, Pr, Sm, Tb, Th, Tm, U, Yb) are determined in geological materials using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The sample is decomposed using a sodium peroxide-sodium hydroxide fusion to ensure complete dissolution of the elements. The digested sample is aspirated into a radio frequency plasma and the resultant ions for each element are separated on a mass to charge ratio and measured using an electron multiplier detector. Data are deemed acceptable if they are ±15% at five times the Lower Limit of Determination (LOD) and the calculated Relative Standard Deviation (RSD) of duplicate samples is no greater than 15%.
